goal: Monitoring figures (MO1): app/monitoring.py with points per timestamp, half-open period windows, tiles, 7-point rolling mean and 30-point spikes, export list (Board gate 183: 7-point mean; gate 184: tile cap 8 with note '8 of N measures', rolling mean includes the current point, spike z uses the population stdev of the previous 30)

acceptance_criteria.text: monitoring.view(columns, typed, mapping, period, settings) returns {'tiles','charts','period','periods':['7','30','90','all'],'latest'}; rows with empty time are dropped, repeated timestamps are averaged per numerical column, points sorted by time
Windows are half-open: current t > last - N days, previous last - 2N < t <= last - N; 'all' has no previous window

One tile per numerical column, capped at 8 (primary numeric first by the apps.MEASURE name rule, then column order); with more numerics the payload carries a note '8 of N measures'; tile has column, latest, min, max, mean, previous, pct (1 decimal, None for 'all', empty previous or previous 0), dir up/down/no change, spark (at most 60 points); tiles of plain columns are flagged so values print without separators

On monitor_rows() period 30: temperature latest 20.0, min 20.0, max 60.0, pct 5.1 up; humidity latest 54, min 50, max 54, pct 0.0 no change; quiet.csv temperature pct -0.4 down; period 'all' gives pct None for every tile; period 7 covers 7 points

Main line chart dict kind 'monitor' with x ISO times, y, mean (7-point trailing, includes the current point, partial at the start) and spike positions (i >= 30, population stdev of the previous 30 > 0, |z| > 3); monitor.csv spike is exactly 2024-04-10, 7-point mean there 28.4286 and last 23.0; quiet.csv spike == []; computed in O(n) so 200,000 rows stay fast; spike points survive stride sampling

monitoring.export(view) returns [tiles table (Column, Latest, Min, Max, Change %), a kind 'line' chart of the main line with x/y data only], ids chart-1..; tests/test_monitoring.py compares with values recomputed by hand from monitor_rows()
